item.title: Implement rate limiter in ratelimit.py per SPEC.md
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, local chat): "Implement the rate limiter described in `SPEC.md` in `ratelimit.py` (the module currently only has stubs). Follow the spec exactly, including its error cases and edge cases; the tests in `test_ratelimit.py` only cover the basics. Keep it dependency-free (standard library only) and commit your work."

Goal: implement `TokenBucket` and `KeyedLimiter` in `ratelimit.py` exactly as `SPEC.md` defines them. Read `SPEC.md` first; it is the contract.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every method, ValueError rule, default, and edge case in SPEC.md is implemented: start full, continuous fractional refill capped at capacity, try_acquire/available/wait_time semantics (wait_time consumes nothing and returns 0.0 when it would succeed now), n validation, clock going backwards leaves state unchanged until the clock passes the latest time already seen, KeyedLimiter per-key buckets created on first use, LRU eviction at max_keys where try_acquire and wait_time both count as use, evicted keys restart full, and len() returns the tracked key count.
- Clock is the injected `clock` callable only; no other time reads.
- Standard library only; no new dependencies.
- Keep existing public names and signatures from the stubs; default clock is time.monotonic.
- Add or extend tests in `test_ratelimit.py` to cover the spec's error cases and edge cases (invalid capacity/refill/n/max_keys, clock regression, fractional tokens, cap at capacity, wait_time math, LRU ordering including use via wait_time, eviction restarting full, len). Run the tests and make them pass.
- Code style: functions under 60 lines, clear names, early-return guard clauses, at least two meaningful asserts or explicit ValueError checks at boundaries, no swallowed exceptions, no unnecessary comments.
- Commit the work on the item's branch with a clear message. Do not push. Do not set git identity overrides; do not add attribution lines to the commit.
- Do not touch files other than ratelimit.py and test_ratelimit.py (SPEC.md stays unchanged).

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier

model_reasons.implement: Spec has several edge cases (clock regression, LRU use via wait_time, eviction semantics) where a subtle slip would hide; high effort for that.

pr.body: Approach: TokenBucket keeps tokens as float, refills from the latest time seen (clock regressions are no-ops), and wait_time computes (n - tokens) / refill_per_sec. KeyedLimiter keeps an OrderedDict of buckets; _bucket() moves the key to the end on use and pops the LRU key before creating a new bucket at max_keys. n is validated in KeyedLimiter before any key is created or evicted. Files: ratelimit.py, test_ratelimit.py only. Checks: python3 -W error -m unittest test_ratelimit -> Ran 23 tests, OK. No linter is configured in the repo; pyflakes is not installed. Review: first reviewer (whole change) failed on non-integer max_keys; fixed in 67949ab with test; second reviewer verified the delta and passed. Assumptions: capacity and refill_per_sec must be > 0 and not NaN; max_keys must be an int >= 1 (SPEC only says < 1 raises); float rounding may make wait_time off by one ulp. Follow-up: bool max_keys (True) is accepted as 1.
pr.summary: Made the rate limiter work. Now: TokenBucket and KeyedLimiter follow SPEC.md, including ValueError rules, clock-regression handling and LRU eviction. Before: stubs raised NotImplementedError (3 original tests error). Now: 23 tests pass.

agt_01M8GMS3NZ4P4K848DQ7YFDG0W:1.description: KeyedLimiter accepts a non-integer max_keys (e.g. 1.5) and then breaks the 'at most max_keys buckets' rule: the check only rejects max_keys < 1, so with max_keys=1.5 a third key drives the bucket count to 2 and the internal assert in _bucket raises AssertionError. Validation should require an integer max_keys >= 1, and a test should cover it. at ratelimit.py:55

risk.why: New feature in a new module behind the existing stub signatures; no change to other code. No security, persistence, or concurrency surface. Tests run and pass; review found one validation bug, fixed and verified.
